In a first-price sealed bid auction with rational bidders, the optimal strategy is to bid strategically below one's true value. Since all values are between $0-$49 and drawn independently, I'll aim to bid close to my value but slightly under, anticipating other bidders will do the same. In a single-round auction with rational bidders, the dominant strategy is to bid slightly less than my true value. Since my value is $17, I want to maximize potential profit. A good strategy is to bid around my value minus a small buffer - say $16.5 - which leaves room for potential profit if I win, but doesn't overpay. This approach balances the risk of overbidding and the opportunity to win.
